transcription.notes: The document has two pages: page 1 is the task sheet, page 2 is the official key headed "Comented results" (printed spelling), attached as the solutions. No points are printed; only times per task. Problem 2's key prints "a) 1.5" and "b) 0.5" without explanation, while the task sheet prints no a)/b) labels; transcribed as printed, no parts or answer inferred. The star charts 4, 5 and 6 referenced in the tasks are not in this document. In the key, the answer marks (X, GC, PN, OC, EN) and the times are printed in red bold and the spectral types (K3II, B8V) in colour; rendered as bold. The answer tick-box rows are rendered as Markdown tables. Problem 5 keeps the printed „wich“ verbatim.

problems.statement: Use your green laser pointer to aim at 3 zodiacal constellations of your choice. (2 min)

solution.statement: Student will have **2 minutes** to accomplish this task.

problems.statement:
Point to $\nu$ Scorpii (***star chart-4***). If you are not able to point at the star you can ask the instructor to do it for you but you will not get points for this. (3 min)

Use 2x barlow + 10mm eyepiece to draw what you see through the eyepiece. You don´t need to mark North . (2 min)

Point your telescope to the star SAO 209318 (***star chart-5***). Notice a small nebulous patch close to that star. Use your 10mm or 10mm + 2x barlow to estimate the distance between the star and the nebulous patch, in arc minutes. (coordinates to SAO 209318 are $\alpha$: 17h50m51s and $\delta$: -37°02’). Express your answer using 0.5’ precision knowing that the field of view of the 10mm eyepiece on this telescope is 24 arcmin or 0.4º. If you are not able to point at the star, the instructor will do it for you but you lose 50% of the points. (2 min pointing, 3 min determining the distance)

answer.note: Official key: ~ 4.5’ (4’18”); 4 to 5 arc minutes count as 100% correct, 3.0 – 3.9 or 5.1 – 6.0 arc minutes as 70% correct.

solution.statement: R: **~ 4.5’** (4’18”). 4 to 5 arc minutes will be considered 100% correct answers. 3.0 – 3.9 or 5.1 – 6.0 arc minutes will be considered 70% correct. **(5 minutes)**
